body_length_chars: proxy for truncation and wire brevity

near_duplicate_of: pointer to surviving record; which record survives a cluster fixes its timestamp

crawl_id: foreign key to R0 for gate error analysis

publication_timestamp_utc: §3 'publication timestamp'; determines the trading day via the 16:00 NY roll

half of title+summary embedding input

backfill_flag: [I] from §3 '2023 portion was backfilled in bulk'
enables every result with and without it

date: trading DATE not instant; tz-aware storage causes off-by-one-day joins

close_adj: adjustment convention UNSTATED: total-return vs price-return differs by ~dividend yield, material against measured effects

ticker: appears in news text; uppercase, no venue prefix

first_price_date: identifies the <126-observation population that triggers the beta<=1 fallback

has_price_history: [S] as '3.4% of articles reference symbols without price history'
delistings skew small => selection is non-random

date: missing sessions shift every CAR spanning them

teacher_label: 7 fields; the target the student imitates

teacher_label.forward_looking: declared but never reported in results

gate_model.prompt_template:
You are a financial-news analyst. You read ONE article about a US-listed company and
return a structured assessment. Return only the JSON object specified at the end.
Do not speculate about future prices. Do not use knowledge of later events.

COMPANY: {ticker} — {company_name}
SOURCE DOMAIN: {source_domain}

ARTICLE TITLE: {title}
ARTICLE BODY: {body}

TASK 1 — RELEVANCE
Is this article genuinely related to {company_name} ({ticker})?
Answer false if the ticker appears only in a list, if the subject is a different issuer,
or if the piece discusses the sector without naming this company's own operations.

TASK 2 — IMPORTANCE
Is this article important enough to retain for event analysis?
Answer false for: pure price recitation with no new fact; sponsored or promotional
content; syndicated duplicates; routine notices restating already-public filings.

TASK 3 — SENTIMENT
Assign exactly one of:
  "Strongly Negative" | "Negative" | "Neutral" | "Positive" | "Strongly Positive"
The direction is that of the article's IMPLICATION FOR THE EQUITY, not the tone of the
prose. Use "Neutral" for articles with no directional content (e.g. an appointment with
no stated market implication, a factual filing notice, a descriptive price recap).

TASK 4 — SUMMARY
Write 2-3 sentences. Preserve every numeric fact VERBATIM: amounts, percentages,
ratios, dates, guidance ranges, share counts.

OUTPUT — exactly this JSON, nothing else:
{
  "related":   true | false,
  "important": true | false,
  "sentiment": "Strongly Negative" | "Negative" | "Neutral" | "Positive" | "Strongly Positive",
  "summary":   "<2-3 sentences>"
}

teacher.prompt_template:
You label financial news articles for an event study. You return ONLY the JSON object
specified below. You do not forecast prices. You do not use knowledge of the article's
date or of any subsequent event.

--- BLOCK 1: ROLE ---
You are a precise financial-event classifier with expertise in corporate finance and
financial journalism. Assign exactly one primary tag from the taxonomy and, when a
second economic event is genuinely present, one secondary tag. Then set the five
binary attributes.

--- BLOCK 2: TAXONOMY (17 DEFINITIONS) ---
{TAXONOMY_BLOCK}
# Each injected entry has the form:
#   <tag name> — <one-sentence definition>
#     include: <criterion 1>; <criterion 2>
#     exclude: <criterion 1>; <criterion 2>
# Mandatory disambiguations to inject:
#   Earnings results vs Guidance, outlook — if both present, primary=Earnings results,
#     secondary=Guidance, outlook.
#   Analyst action vs Price commentary — Analyst action requires a sell-side rating,
#     target, or estimate change; Price commentary is content ABOUT the price move itself.
#   Macro through stock — macro or sector news whose relevance to this issuer is
#     inferential rather than direct.
#   Other corporate — a genuine corporate event not covered by any other tag.
#   Price commentary / Promotional content are the two junk categories: use them rather
#     than forcing price-descriptive or promotional text into a real event tag.

--- BLOCK 3: ATTRIBUTES (5 BINARY DEFINITIONS) ---
{ATTRIBUTE_BLOCK}
# scheduled       : was the event on a pre-announced calendar date?
# forward_looking : does the article's primary content concern future periods?
# primary_source  : does it carry a company/regulator/official release rather than a
#                   journalistic reconstruction?
# quantified      : does it contain at least one number CENTRAL to the event
#                   (amount, ratio, percentage, date, guidance range)?
# rumor           : is the central claim explicitly attributed to unnamed sources
#                   ("people familiar", "reportedly", "said to be")?

--- BLOCK 4: EXEMPLARS (4 FEW-SHOT PAIRS) ---
{EXEMPLARS_BLOCK}
# Each injected exemplar is: article title + body, then its completed 7-field label.
# Coverage: a quantified scheduled earnings report; a rumor; an unquantified product
# launch; one junk-category article (Price commentary).

--- BLOCK 5: OUTPUT CONTRACT ---
Return exactly the JSON object, with no additional keys and no prose:
{
  "primary_tag":   "<one of the 17 tag names>",
  "secondary_tag": "<one of the 17 tag names, or \"none\">",
  "scheduled":       true | false,
  "forward_looking": true | false,
  "primary_source":  true | false,
  "quantified":      true | false,
  "rumor":           true | false
}

--- ARTICLE ---
TITLE: {title}
BODY:  {body}

DEF40.rationale: The reported 1.35 gross Sharpe pins this convention; the exact arithmetic implies sqrt(252) scaling with a zero risk-free

figure_4_tag_map.y_axis: 17 tags sorted by adjusted post-long drift

figure_5_cumulative_portfolios.hedge_note: each strategy beta-hedged with a sized index position

methodological_notes.identification_logic: [S] Difference-in-differences in event time. Treated = signed coverage; control = neutral coverage, conditioned on annual size tercile. Parallel paths is an ASSUMPTION, tested only by the tag-matched baseline variant, which weakens capital returns and zeroes the launch estimate (those two tags' neutral coverage selects dividend payers and promoted small caps).
methodological_notes.benchmark_misfit_cancellation: [S] Baseline and events are measured against the SAME single-beta benchmark, so additive misfit cancels; a richer factor model would shrink the baseline itself and leave adjusted estimates essentially unchanged.
methodological_notes.sign_after_differencing_algebra: [S] Because s is applied AFTER differencing, the baseline enters as -s*b. One negative drift therefore produces apparent reversal after good news (s=+1) and apparent continuation after bad news (s=-1). At 73% positive sentiment the pooled average is dominated by the reversal case.
methodological_notes.mirror_image_diagnostic: [S] Raw [+6,+20] drift is -0.62% after positive and +0.63% after negative news: near-exact mirrors of one constant |b| ~ 0.62%. If your pipeline does not reproduce this mirror, the baseline is misspecified and all downstream results are void.
methodological_notes.generated_regressor_direction: [S] Re-estimating the baseline inside every bootstrap draw yields the same or slightly stronger significance, so holding it fixed is CONSERVATIVE. This is the correct direction of error.
methodological_notes.frozen_centroid_consequence: [I] Because story centroids are frozen, an evolving story (rumor -> signed deal) is re-opened as NEW. This is why the rumor analysis CANNOT link by story id and must link by next same-tag non-rumor event — importing that proxy's weakness.
methodological_notes.provenance_tag_correlation: [I] Max-softmax confidence is higher for frequent classes, so the >=0.8 gate routes RARE tags to the teacher. Hence label_source is not independent of tag and the teacher-only robustness column is compositionally selected. Signs survive; the column warrants a caveat.
methodological_notes.anticipation_vs_reporting: [S] Sentiment is assigned to prose written about moves as well as before them. The NEW-only rerun quantifies this: earnings pre-window +1.41% -> +1.02%, i.e. follow-up coverage inflates measured anticipation by roughly one third. The claim is descriptive, not causal.
methodological_notes.two_hop_label_error: [S] The 10,000-article validation set is itself teacher-labelled, so 87.5%/94.0% are agreement with a pseudo-oracle. Error is two-hop (human -> teacher -> student). A human gold set is the missing control.
methodological_notes.beta_fallback_asymmetry: [I] The beta<=1 rule assigns full market exposure to thin-history stocks — i.e. small, recently listed names, exactly where the headline reversals live. Not stress-tested in the paper.
methodological_notes.dollar_volume_distortion: [I] adjusted_close * raw_volume is NOT true dollar volume, since adjusted prices are rescaled by cumulative adjustment factors. Tercile membership therefore inherits a distortion for stocks with long split/dividend histories.
methodological_notes.width_survives_where_direction_does_not: [S] Volatility ratios are self-referential (a stock vs its own typical day), so the background drift cancels. This is why the width results are robust to the critique that demolishes the direction results.
methodological_notes.lookahead_immunity: [S] No network in the study ever sees a return. The teacher labels and never forecasts; its prompt excludes date and price. Exposure is confined to pretraining on historically published text, not to any outcome variable.
methodological_notes.volume_arithmetic_inconsistency: [I] '>250,000 URLs/day' across ~850 trading days implies >=2e8 URLs, against a stated total of '>70 million'. Both cannot describe the whole sample; plausible readings are a ramping daily rate or a counts-vs-retains distinction.
methodological_notes.teacher_call_arithmetic: [I] 29,472 + 99,991 + 10,000 = 139,463, against a reported 139,464. A one-call discrepancy, immaterial to both dollar figures, but present — evidence the cost ledger was reconstructed rather than exported.
methodological_notes.economic_significance_verdict: [S] The fade portfolio (15.8%, Sharpe 1.35) is indistinguishable from shorting every covered small cap (15.9%, Sharpe 1.35); curves superimposed. The entire fade edge IS the background drift the estimator subtracts. Following legal news dies at 10 bps. Residual tag-map alphas are real but thin against plausible costs.

DEF1.rationale: Smallest Azure-hosted model consistent with day-by-day vendor pipeline cost

DEF2.rationale: Ubiquitous sentence encoder with a 384-d output that supports whitening

DEF3.rationale: §3 says 'to 2026' without a date; the paper's submission (Nov 2026) implies mid-2026 availability

DEF4.rationale: Preserves syndication chains while collapsing tracking-only duplicates

DEF5.rationale: Hamming distance 3 on SimHash-64 is standard and conservative

DEF6.rationale: Preserves the true publication timestamp over fetch-order noise

DEF7.rationale: Paper does not report this; reproduction records whatever it yields

DEF8.rationale: 17 tags + explicit 'none' is the natural formulation; the 17-sigmoid alternative is executed as an ablation

DEF10.rationale: Four outputs plus a 2-3 sentence summary

DEF11.rationale: Symmetric about zero; required because event impact = mean of article sentiment and must average correctly

DEF12.rationale: Typical 2-3 sentence summary; governs the lossy-compression ratio for the story embedder

DEF13.rationale: Prevents non-English contamination of `Neutral` sentiment and `quantified` attribute

DEF14.rationale: Determinism as far as the API allows; no seed exposed by gpt-5-mini

DEF15.rationale: Balances full-article coverage against $0.0002/call economics; establishes the teacher-student input-length mismatch (H2)

DEF16.rationale: Body preserves numerals; title alone loses them; title+summary compounds the gate's compression and would attenuate the `quantified` effect

DEF17.rationale: RoBERTa trained without NSP, so [CLS] is not a learned sentence summary; mean pooling is the correct default for a RoBERTa-family encoder

DEF18.rationale: Head truncation + 96-token budget for numeral-bearing sentences; preserves the `quantified` attribute, which carries the paper's headline economic finding

DEF19.rationale: Standard supervised fine-tuning of a DistilRoBERTa multi-task head; inverse-frequency weighting is necessary because tag counts span >25×

DEF20.rationale: Down-weights the auxiliary heads relative to the primary tag; the disjunction between primary and attribute performance (87.5% vs 92-99%) implies the fine-tuning balance was struck in this direction

DEF21.rationale: Deterministic RNG for the 29,472 bootstrap sample draw and any downstream stochastic step

DEF22.rationale: Max over the primary-tag softmax; natural confidence scalar, and the frequency-correlation consequence is handled separately by the rare-class quota

DEF23.rationale: At least 500 routed items per tag guarantees the sparse tags attain stable learned representations

DEF24.rationale: Anisotropy in raw contextual embeddings makes a raw 0.80 cosine threshold uninterpretable; whitening is the corrective

DEF25.rationale: Consistent with §4.2's bracketed '(threshold 0.80)' phrasing, which is directly the single-link component rule; the frozen-centroid cross-day step prevents the chaining pathology that usually argues against single-link

DEF26.rationale: Same threshold as intra-day; lowering it risks chaining across semantically adjacent but distinct stories

DEF27.rationale: Deterministic tie-breaking for equidistant day-clusters; without it the event table is non-reproducible

DEF28.rationale: Makes §4.2's 'where continued matches become rare' operational; a 10th-percentile cutoff is a standard defensible rule

DEF30.rationale: Caps set to twice the measured mean lifetime for the 12 tags whose caps the paper does not state; generous enough to avoid truncating live stories, tight enough to prevent over-linking

DEF31.rationale: Literal 16:00 is faithful to the paper's stated rule and preserves the reported cardinalities; the economic-fidelity alternative (use `session_close`) is run as a bounded sensitivity

DEF32.rationale: Impact = 0 with mixed-polarity articles is a genuine gap in the paper; majority-polarity resolves most cases, true ties are flagged `is_mixed` and treated as robustness

DEF33.rationale: The paper's running-total figure (+0.579% → +0.204%) is a simple sum of daily AR; no annualization implied

DEF34.rationale: §4.3's phrase 'the mean abnormal return of neutral events' is most naturally event-weighted; the calendar-weighted variant is a plausible alternative

DEF35.rationale: Standard defaults; the studentized variant is run as a sensitivity for boundary cases

DEF36.rationale: Sparse tags (guidance, competition, capital returns, M&A) require a wild-cluster check against bootstrap degeneracy

DEF37.rationale: TRUE dollar volume, not the adjusted-price × raw-volume product distorted by cumulative adjustment factors

DEF38.rationale: Names with fewer than 20 trading days in a year are bucketed by the previous year's assignment; prevents short-window noise

DEF39.rationale: §5.1 says 'prior month'; 21 trading days is the standard financial-definition conversion

DEF40.rationale: The reported 1.35 gross Sharpe pins this convention; the exact arithmetic implies sqrt(252) scaling with a zero risk-free

DEF41.rationale: Rare-tag enrichment in the teacher-labeled set biases the column's composition; reweighting restores representativeness

DEF42.rationale: Uniform denominator across the pipeline; median variant is a sensitivity

DEF43.value: rule-based classifier by known wire/aggregator/retail/mainstream/portal domains
DEF43.rationale: The paper publishes no mapping; a rule-based classifier is the only faithful reproduction, and its classification of each outlet must be reported

DEF44.value: 510-item tag-stratified adjudicated sample with two annotators and third-annotator conflict resolution
DEF44.rationale: Directly addresses the two-hop pseudo-oracle acknowledged in §7; per-tag precision/recall bounds the boundary q-values

DEF45.rationale: §5.3's 1.09M NEW-only count does not reconcile with the 55%-follow-up × 1.86M arithmetic under the natural denominators; the reproduction must document the denominator it uses
